title: How to Manage Item Inventory Across Properties
summary: See how to track item inventory — furniture, supplies, equipment — across a short-stay property portfolio.
body_markdown:
Managing item inventory across properties means each unit's furniture, supplies, and equipment connect to a structured record, with replenishment and loss tracked consistently — instead of a mental inventory that only the on-site cleaner or manager holds. In **Jestor** , this uses the same structured stock table applied to physical goods generally.


Short-stay properties accumulate inventory needs — linens, kitchen supplies, welcome amenities — that are easy to under-track until something's missing mid-stay and there's no record of what should have been there.


## What untracked property inventory costs


- No record of what should be in a property, making loss or theft hard to detect
- Replenishment happening reactively, only after staff notice something's missing
- No consolidated view of inventory costs across the whole portfolio
- Inconsistent stocking standards between different properties


## How structured inventory management works


- Each property's expected inventory connects to its own structured record
- Automations can flag low-stock or replenishment needs based on turnover frequency
- Costs connect back to the property, supporting per-unit cost analysis
- Consistent standards can be enforced through a shared inventory template


## Why Jestor fits this use case


- Inventory data stays connected to the specific property, not tracked informally
- Automated replenishment flags reduce reliance on staff noticing shortages
- Dashboards consolidate inventory cost and status across the whole portfolio
- A shared template keeps stocking standards consistent as the portfolio grows


Untracked inventory Structured inventory management


Mental tracking, easy to miss shortages Structured records with automated flags

## Frequently Asked Questions


**Can replenishment needs be flagged automatically?** Yes, based on thresholds or turnover frequency you define. More at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Can inventory standards be kept consistent across properties?** Yes, through a shared inventory template.


**Does this track cost per property?** Yes, inventory costs connect to the specific property's record.
